scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: the Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose in September as third-quarter GDP beat expectations
lines.note: THE DOOR: the price named by its instrument ('the Fed's preferred gauge'); no cause in the hed
lines.zWhy: a gauge rising is a price not yet coming down

lines.quote: rose further away from the central bank's target in September as consumers face price pressures
lines.note: the lede: the number measured as distance from the Fed's 2%, not from a year ago or from the pump
lines.zWhy: further from target is a price moving the wrong way

lines.quote: PCE +0.5% on the month, +3.6% on the year in September — in line with LSEG's economists
lines.note: THE NUMBER, DATED AND SIZED — the page's lowest line; the deal's price leg as an index
lines.zWhy: three-point-six is the price up, not down

lines.quote: core PCE, excluding food and energy, +0.3% on the month, +3.1% on the year
lines.note: the only 'energy' on the page is the word that excludes it from the measure — method-occluded in one clause
lines.zWhy: a core still rising is a price up beyond fuel

lines.quote: policymakers focus on headline PCE toward a 2% target, but view core as the better indicator
lines.note: the instrument explained; the object (what rose, and why) replaced by which measure the Fed prefers
lines.zWhy: a target not yet reached reads slightly against the cure

lines.quote: headline PCE up from 3.4% to 3.6% since August; core from 3% to 3.1%
lines.zWhy: a rise on August is a price still climbing

lines.quote: goods prices +3.9% on the year, services +3.5%
lines.note: goods and services sized; fuel not broken out
lines.zWhy: goods near four percent is a price not yet down

lines.quote: the savings rate 3.8%, down from 4% in August — from 6.2% at the April 2025 peak and 5.6% in January
lines.note: THE CONSUMER DRAWING DOWN — the page's one line on who pays the price; the AP wire has the same fact as 'tapping savings or credit'
lines.zWhy: savings falling is a price paid out of reserves

lines.quote: while inflation moved further from the 2% target, third-quarter GDP grew more than expected
lines.note: the pivot — the price's rise bracketed by growth
lines.zWhy: further from target reads against the cure, growth reads neither way

lines.quote: GDP 3.4% annualized in Q3 against 3.2% expected (BEA advance estimate; two revisions to come)
lines.note: growth — off the price's axis; dated and sized
lines.zWhy: a growth number reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: today's in-line PCE report offered little surprise — but inflation remains stubborn at its highest since May
lines.note: THE TITLE — the number read as a surprise that did not happen; 'stubborn' is the price given a temperament
lines.zWhy: stubborn since May is a price not coming down

lines.quote: consumers drove Q3 growth; federal consumption at its highest in at least five years; resilient demand that does not ease inflation
lines.note: the consumer's resilience read as the price's cause — the pump nowhere
lines.zWhy: demand that does not ease inflation reads neither way on the cure

lines.quote: a seemingly indefatigable U.S. consumer and a nascent AI investment boom; growth well above trend
lines.note: the page's most denominated line — two adjectives and a boom, no price
lines.zWhy: a boom reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: as oil prices spike and financial conditions tighten, headwinds should cool activity by year end; the Fed's no-hike decision questioned
lines.note: THE CAUSE, ONCE — 'oil prices spike' is the only sentence on the page that touches the war's price; it arrives as a headwind to growth, not as the object
lines.zWhy: oil spiking is the crunch not yet relieved

lines.quote: Warsh was reluctant to signal at yesterday's FOMC; a December hike expected, perhaps one more in 2027
lines.note: the clock on this page is the Fed's — December, 2027; the holder's 'really fast' is not here to compare
lines.zWhy: a hike expected is a price the Fed does not expect to fall on its own

lines.quote: markets expect a 25-basis-point hike in December, to 4.00–4.25%
lines.zWhy: a priced hike is a price not expected down by December

lines.quote: FedWatch: 79.6% for a December hike, from 84.2% yesterday and 73.3% a week ago
lines.note: the odds, dated three ways — the page's own trace line
lines.zWhy: four in five on a hike is a price read as staying up
